quests.hint: Pieces of work a tutor sets you to complete on your own.
quests.explanation: Assignments, essays and presentations are all things students hand in, so the deadline gives nothing away. Assignments is stressed in the middle: a-SSIGN-ments.
quests.textToSpeak: I've got two assignments due at the end of the month.
quests.textWithBlanks: I've got two ___ due at the end of the month.

quests.instruction: Something's missing! Grab the right brick to fix the sentence.
quests.hint: The subject that designs bridges, engines and machines.
quests.explanation: Engineering, economics and architecture are all degree subjects, and each is several syllables long, so you cannot use word length as a clue. Listen for the vowel at the very beginning.
quests.textToSpeak: She's studying engineering at a university up north.
quests.textWithBlanks: She's studying ___ at a university up north.

quests.instruction: Something's missing! Grab the right brick to fix the sentence.
quests.hint: Only just, with very little room to spare.
quests.explanation: Barely passed means you only just succeeded, but nearly passed means you actually failed. One quiet word completely reverses the result, which is why these adverbs matter so much.
quests.textToSpeak: I barely passed the first test, but the retake went much better.
quests.textWithBlanks: I ___ passed the first test, but the retake went much better.

quests.instruction: Something's missing! Grab the right brick to fix the sentence.
quests.hint: The screen stops responding and nothing moves.
quests.explanation: Freezing, crashing and restarting describe three different computer problems, and all three follow keeps naturally. Keeps plus -ing means it happens again and again.
quests.textToSpeak: My laptop keeps freezing whenever I open too many tabs.
quests.textWithBlanks: My laptop keeps ___ whenever I open too many tabs.

quests.instruction: Something's missing! Grab the right brick to fix the sentence.
quests.hint: Text you click to open a web page.
quests.explanation: Send me the link, the file or the folder are all everyday requests, and each is short and easy to miss. A link points to something online, while a file is the thing itself.
quests.textToSpeak: Can you send me the link? I'll download it later.
quests.textWithBlanks: Can you send me the ___? I'll download it later.

quests.instruction: Something's missing! Grab the right brick to fix the sentence.
quests.hint: To set a completely new one because the old one is lost.
quests.explanation: Reset is what you do when you have forgotten a password, while change and confirm are things you do when you still know it. All three are two-syllable verbs in the same slot.
quests.textToSpeak: I forgot my password, so I had to reset it.
quests.textWithBlanks: I forgot my password, so I had to ___ it.

quests.instruction: Something's missing! Grab the right brick to fix the sentence.
quests.hint: The bill for the power that runs your lights.
quests.explanation: Electricity, water and internet bills all arrive regularly and can all go up. Electricity is five syllables with the stress in the middle, which makes it feel faster than it looks.
quests.textToSpeak: The electricity bill's gone up again this quarter.
quests.textWithBlanks: The ___ bill's gone up again this quarter.

quests.instruction: Something's missing! Grab the right brick to fix the sentence.
quests.hint: Two times, when it should have been one.
quests.explanation: Charged me twice, extra and again are three different complaints, and only one of them means you were billed two separate times. This is exactly the kind of detail you must catch on a support call.
quests.textToSpeak: They charged me twice for the same order.
quests.textWithBlanks: They charged me ___ for the same order.

quests.instruction: Something's missing! Grab the right brick to fix the sentence.
quests.hint: The first large payment you make towards a home.
quests.explanation: Save up for means collect money slowly over time, and people save up for a deposit, a holiday or a car. A deposit is the part you pay at the start, not the whole price.
quests.textToSpeak: I'm trying to save up for a deposit on a flat.
quests.textWithBlanks: I'm trying to save up for a ___ on a flat.

quests.instruction: Something's missing! Grab the right brick to fix the sentence.
quests.hint: Nothing can get through at all.
quests.explanation: Blocked, flooded and jammed all describe a road you cannot use, but for different reasons. Blocked ends in a hard 'kt' cluster that often disappears before the next word.
quests.textToSpeak: There's been an accident, so the road's completely blocked.
quests.textWithBlanks: There's been an accident, so the road's completely ___.

quests.instruction: Something's missing! Grab the right brick to fix the sentence.
quests.hint: Unable to move, with cars all around you.
quests.explanation: Stuck in traffic, caught in traffic and held up in traffic are all real expressions that mean the same thing. When several options are equally correct English, the audio is your only route to the answer.
quests.textToSpeak: I got stuck in traffic for over an hour.
quests.textWithBlanks: I got ___ in traffic for over an hour.

quests.instruction: Something's missing! Grab the right brick to fix the sentence.
quests.hint: Put on instead of the normal train service.
quests.explanation: A replacement bus runs when the trains are not, while a shuttle bus and an express bus are ordinary services. Station announcements use this word constantly, so it is worth knowing well.
quests.textToSpeak: The replacement bus service takes about twice as long.
quests.textWithBlanks: The ___ bus service takes about twice as long.

quests.instruction: Something's missing! Grab the right brick to fix the sentence.
quests.hint: Relaxed, and not easily upset by anything.
quests.explanation: Easy-going, hard-working and well-organised are all two-part adjectives used to describe character, and they share the same rhythm. Only the second half of the sentence hints at the meaning, and only faintly.
quests.textToSpeak: He's really easy-going, so almost nothing bothers him.
quests.textWithBlanks: He's really ___, so almost nothing bothers him.

quests.instruction: Something's missing! Grab the right brick to fix the sentence.
quests.hint: It is her general habit to do this.
quests.explanation: Tends to worry describes a habit, seems to worry describes an impression, and refuses to worry means the complete opposite. One small verb changes the whole picture of the person.
quests.textToSpeak: She tends to worry about things she can't control.
quests.textWithBlanks: She ___ to worry about things she can't control.

quests.instruction: Something's missing! Grab the right brick to fix the sentence.
quests.hint: To keep something in your mind so you do not fail to do it.
quests.explanation: Never remembers and never forgets describe opposite people, yet the sentence around them is identical. Listen right through the middle of the sentence, not just the ends.
quests.textToSpeak: My flatmate never remembers to lock the door.
quests.textWithBlanks: My flatmate never ___ to lock the door.

quests.instruction: Something's missing! Grab the right brick to fix the sentence.
quests.hint: Travelling somewhere else and staying there.
quests.explanation: Go away means leave home for a trip, while go out means leave the house for the evening. Camping names the activity instead, so all three fit but describe different plans.
quests.textToSpeak: We're thinking of going away for the bank holiday.
quests.textWithBlanks: We're thinking of going ___ for the bank holiday.

quests.instruction: Something's missing! Grab the right brick to fix the sentence.
quests.hint: Having no other commitments at that time.
quests.explanation: Are you free, are you around and are you in are three natural ways of asking the same thing, and all three are one short syllable. This is a polite way to check before inviting someone.
quests.textToSpeak: Are you free on Saturday, or have you got plans?
quests.textWithBlanks: Are you ___ on Saturday, or have you got plans?

quests.instruction: Something's missing! Grab the right brick to fix the sentence.
quests.hint: Saying this means you insist on paying.
quests.explanation: It's my treat, my round and my turn all mean I am paying, with round used mainly for drinks. The reason given afterwards works for any of them, so you must catch the noun itself.
quests.textToSpeak: It's my treat this time. You paid for lunch last week.
quests.textWithBlanks: It's my ___ this time. You paid for lunch last week.

quests.instruction: Something's missing! Grab the right brick to fix the sentence.
quests.hint: The hot box you bake things in.
quests.explanation: Take it out of the oven, the fridge or the pan are all normal kitchen instructions. Out of the is reduced to something like 'outtha', so the noun arrives very quickly.
quests.textToSpeak: Give it another five minutes, then take it out of the oven.
quests.textWithBlanks: Give it another five minutes, then take it out of the ___.

quests.instruction: Something's missing! Grab the right brick to fix the sentence.
quests.hint: The white seasoning that makes food taste less flat.
quests.explanation: Salt, pepper and lemon are all things you add at the end of cooking, and a bit more works with each. Salt is short, and the 'l' almost disappears in many accents.
quests.textToSpeak: This needs a bit more salt, I think.
quests.textWithBlanks: This needs a bit more ___, I think.

quests.instruction: Something's missing! Grab the right brick to fix the sentence.
quests.hint: How hot the cooker is set.
quests.explanation: Turn the heat down, the gas down and the temperature down are all things a cook might say, and they mean roughly the same. Boil over means liquid rising and spilling out of the pan.
quests.textToSpeak: Don't let it boil over. Turn the heat down a bit.
quests.textWithBlanks: Don't let it boil over. Turn the ___ down a bit.

quests.instruction: Something's missing! Grab the right brick to fix the sentence.
quests.hint: In another country.
quests.explanation: Living abroad, alone and nearby are three very different situations, and the rest of the sentence supports all of them. Abroad has its stress on the second syllable, so the first part is almost silent.
quests.textToSpeak: He's been living abroad for the past three years.
quests.textWithBlanks: He's been living ___ for the past three years.

quests.instruction: Something's missing! Grab the right brick to fix the sentence.
quests.hint: Given jobs to, not taken jobs away from.
quests.explanation: Hired and fired differ by a single sound at the front, but they are opposite news for a company. Trained sits between them as a third realistic possibility.
quests.textToSpeak: They've hired three new designers this month.
quests.textWithBlanks: They've ___ three new designers this month.

quests.instruction: Something's missing! Grab the right brick to fix the sentence.
quests.hint: From what people say, though the speaker was not sure before.
quests.explanation: Apparently signals second-hand information, obviously signals something expected, and luckily signals relief. These comment words come at the start of a clause and are said fast, so they are easily lost.
quests.textToSpeak: I thought she'd already left, but apparently she's still here.
quests.textWithBlanks: I thought she'd already left, but ___ she's still here.

quests.instruction: Something's missing! Grab the right brick to fix the sentence.
quests.hint: To say again, officially, that something is definitely agreed.
quests.explanation: Just to confirm means we already agreed, just to check means I am not sure, and just to clarify means something was unclear. The three openings set up very different conversations.
quests.textToSpeak: Just to confirm, we're meeting at ten rather than eleven.
quests.textWithBlanks: Just to ___, we're meeting at ten rather than eleven.

quests.instruction: Something's missing! Grab the right brick to fix the sentence.
quests.hint: Added to the email as a separate document.
quests.explanation: Attached, included and updated are all things you can do with figures before sending them, and each ends in the same weak -ed sound. Attached is the standard word for a file sent with an email.
quests.textToSpeak: I've attached the figures you asked for yesterday.
quests.textWithBlanks: I've ___ the figures you asked for yesterday.

quests.instruction: Something's missing! Grab the right brick to fix the sentence.
quests.hint: A chain of replies on the same subject.
quests.explanation: Copy me in on that thread, that email or that invite are all normal office requests. A thread is the whole conversation, not just one message.
quests.textToSpeak: Could you copy me in on that thread with the supplier?
quests.textWithBlanks: Could you copy me in on that ___ with the supplier?

quests.instruction: Something's missing! Grab the right brick to fix the sentence.
quests.hint: This tiny word makes 'look' mean investigate.
quests.explanation: Look into means investigate, look after means take care of, and look over means check quickly. The verb is identical in all three, so the tiny word after it carries the entire meaning.
quests.textToSpeak: I'll look into it and get back to you tomorrow.
quests.textWithBlanks: I'll look ___ it and get back to you tomorrow.

quests.instruction: Something's missing! Grab the right brick to fix the sentence.
quests.hint: A journey somewhere, planned in advance.
quests.explanation: Call something off means cancel it, and the object sits between the two parts: call the trip off. A wedding or a launch could be called off just as easily.
quests.textToSpeak: We had to call the trip off at the last minute.
quests.textWithBlanks: We had to call the ___ off at the last minute.

quests.instruction: Something's missing! Grab the right brick to fix the sentence.
quests.hint: Growing into a bigger and bigger heap.
quests.explanation: Piling up, building up and adding up all describe things increasing, but piling up suggests a physical stack of unfinished work. Have been is squeezed to almost nothing before the main verb.
quests.textToSpeak: Things have been piling up since I got back from leave.
quests.textWithBlanks: Things have been ___ up since I got back from leave.
